title: Report Generation Module Architecture
text: Report Generation Module Architecture
description: This page details the architecture and functionality of the Report Generation Module. The module fetches transactional data, applies business filters, and generates reports in both PDF and Excel. The backend is built using Spring Boot with microservice principles, exposing endpoints for generating, previewing, and downloading reports. Frontend will provide dynamic filtering and grouping features. Error tracking is integrated with Splunk and ELK. Reports are cached for 24 hours using Redis for performance optimization.
acceptance_criteria: Reports must be generated in under 10 seconds for 10,000 records., Support download in both PDF and Excel formats with company branding., Include dynamic filters like date range, client ID, transaction type., Must include pagination and total counts in reports., Only authorized users can trigger report generation., Audit log entries must be generated for every report request., Errors must return clear messages and codes (e.g., 400, 403, 500).

title: Data Ingestion Pipeline (Client Reference Data)
text: Data Ingestion Pipeline (Client Reference Data)
description: This page documents the design of the data ingestion service for client reference data. Data is fetched from an upstream vendor API and passed through a validation and transformation layer. Valid records are upserted into MongoDB. A backup of the raw feed is saved to an S3 bucket. Ingestion failures trigger alerts via PagerDuty. Kafka topics are used to notify downstream systems. The pipeline is built using Spring Batch with retry logic, schema validation, and duplicate detection.
acceptance_criteria: Service should poll vendor API every 15 minutes., Validation errors must be logged and skipped, not block the batch., Each batch must be stored as a backup in S3 with timestamp., Kafka message must be published for each valid record ingested., Deduplication must prevent inserting existing records., Dashboard should display ingestion rate and error count., SLA: 95% of records processed in <1 min; alert if breached.

title: Authentication and Authorization Microservice
text:
Authentication and Authorization Microservice
The purpose of this Confluence page is to design the authentication and role-based authorization microservice. It supports JWT-based login with refresh tokens and LDAP fallback. Roles are managed via an internal admin dashboard. Service integrates with Keycloak for OAuth2.0 compliance. All token activity is audited. The microservice is containerized using Docker and deployed in a separate namespace to reduce blast radius.

The microservice is containerized using Docker and deployed in a separate namespace to reduce blast radius.

title: User Preferences Service
text:
User Preferences Service
This page outlines the user preferences microservice that stores configuration such as theme, language, and notification preferences. The service provides CRUD operations and integrates with MongoDB. Preferences are loaded during login and cached using Redis. Preference changes trigger event publication to allow real-time updates in the UI. API layer is secured using OAuth 2.0 access tokens.

title: Trade Reconciliation Service
text:
Trade Reconciliation Service
The reconciliation service compares internal trades against broker feed to identify mismatches. Differences are highlighted via a UI, and reconciliation history is maintained. The service provides APIs to fetch match status, update trade states, and export results. It runs in batch mode every night. Historical reconciliation data is archived in a cold storage system after 90 days.

title: Notification Service (Email/SMS/Slack)
text:
Notification Service (Email/SMS/Slack)
This Confluence page captures the design and functionality of a centralized notification system. It supports sending emails, SMS, and Slack messages based on triggers from upstream services. Templates are customizable. Throttling and retries are built-in. Logs are persisted to ElasticSearch. Notification preferences are respected at all times, with fallback channels configured.

title: Audit Logging Framework
text:
Audit Logging Framework
The audit logging framework ensures traceability for user and system actions. It supports structured logs, JSON format, and integration with ELK stack. Logs are stored with user ID, timestamp, IP, and request context. A masking layer is applied to hide sensitive fields. Logs are queryable via Kibana dashboards for compliance reviews.

title: Client Onboarding Workflow
text:
Client Onboarding Workflow
This document defines the multi-step workflow for client onboarding, including KYC document upload, digital signature, and internal approvals. The workflow is powered by a Camunda BPM engine. Email notifications are sent for pending actions. Status is tracked via a dashboard. The frontend offers a form-based wizard interface for smooth onboarding.

title: Data Retention Policy Implementation
text:
Data Retention Policy Implementation
The purpose of this document is to define how data retention rules are applied across all services. Each data category has its own TTL policy, ranging from 7 days to 7 years. The deletion is automated via scheduled jobs that archive or purge old data. Legal hold and audit exclusion lists are respected. Configuration is maintained via YAML files version-controlled in Git.

title: API Gateway Setup and Routing Rules
text:
API Gateway Setup and Routing Rules
This page outlines the setup of an API Gateway using Kong to handle traffic routing, security, and logging across all services. Features include rate limiting, IP whitelisting, JWT auth, and CORS configuration. APIs are documented using OpenAPI and exposed via Swagger UI. Gateway metrics are collected via Prometheus for performance monitoring.

title: Exception Handling Strategy for Microservices
text: Exception Handling Strategy for Microservices
description: This Confluence page outlines a consistent exception handling strategy across all backend microservices. Each service implements a global error handler that classifies exceptions into client errors (4xx), server errors (5xx), and custom business exceptions. A standard error response schema includes error code, message, and correlation ID. Alerts are triggered on critical failures and logged in ELK. Developers are advised to use functional-style try-catch blocks to manage downstream dependencies, including database and third-party APIs.
acceptance_criteria: All 4xx and 5xx errors must return a standard JSON error format., Each error must include a unique correlation ID in the response., Unhandled exceptions must be caught by the global handler., Stack traces should not be exposed to the client., Critical 5xx errors must trigger Slack alerts via webhook., All errors must be logged to ELK with trace-level metadata., Retry logic must apply only to idempotent operations.

title: File Upload and Virus Scanning Module
text:
File Upload and Virus Scanning Module
This module enables users to upload documents, images, and PDFs as part of workflows such as onboarding and KYC. Files are scanned for viruses using ClamAV before being accepted. Uploaded files are stored securely in AWS S3 with encrypted paths and signed URLs. Maximum upload size is 20MB per file. Progress bars and drag-drop support are provided in the UI. Invalid files are rejected with user-friendly messages and are not persisted.

Invalid files are rejected with user-friendly messages and are not persisted.

title: Real-Time Dashboard with WebSockets
text: Real-Time Dashboard with WebSockets
description: This document explains the implementation of a real-time metrics dashboard for operational teams. The dashboard receives live updates via WebSocket pushed from backend services using a publish-subscribe mechanism. The backend maintains client sessions, periodically sends health checks, and disconnects inactive clients after timeout. The UI is built in React with dynamic charts rendered using Chart.js. All incoming data is sanitized before rendering to prevent XSS attacks.
acceptance_criteria: WebSocket must support bi-directional messaging over secure (wss) protocol., Dashboard must auto-refresh without page reload., Inactivity timeout should disconnect clients after 15 minutes., Display latency < 1s between event trigger and UI update., Charts must auto-scale and support zoom/filter controls., All WebSocket payloads must be schema validated., Provide fallback to REST polling if WebSocket fails.

title: Multi-Tenant SaaS Architecture Guidelines
text: Multi-Tenant SaaS Architecture Guidelines
description: This page lays out design principles for building a multi-tenant SaaS platform. Tenants are logically isolated at the database level with row-level access control and shared schema. All configurations such as themes, limits, and API keys are scoped to the tenant context. The authentication layer includes tenant-aware token issuance. Audit logs and metrics are also tagged per tenant. Tenant provisioning is automated through Terraform scripts. Resource limits are applied using Kubernetes quotas.
acceptance_criteria: Each request must carry a valid tenant ID in the header., All database queries must filter by tenant ID., Audit logs and metrics must include tenant-specific tags., Kubernetes resource quotas must restrict per-tenant CPU and memory., Provisioning pipeline must support creating tenant infra in <2 mins., Support per-tenant custom branding in UI via config service., Error messages must never leak tenant identifiers.

title: PDF Generation Engine using Headless Chrome
text:
PDF Generation Engine using Headless Chrome
This Confluence page describes the service responsible for generating high-quality PDFs from HTML templates using Puppeteer (headless Chrome). The service queues PDF jobs, supports batch export, and allows embedding charts and dynamic elements. All templates are customizable and pulled from a config repo. Rendered PDFs are uploaded to S3 and linked in user portals. The engine auto-scales using horizontal pod autoscaler based on job queue size.
